text:
maria_research: nightly evals: big spike in codegen stop-seq failures for redwood-3b-ptq-int8 after last PTQ rollout. failure rate went from 1.2% -> 9.8% on codegen promptset :frowning:

alex_infra: grabbing the nightly artifact and logs now. which commit rolled the PTQ?

maria_research: PTQ build 2026-03-12 (ci/artifacts/ptq-20260312). regression starts in that build. metrics attached in the dashboard link: https://redwood.internal/evals/ptq-nightly/2470123456

sahil_eval: repro on my laptop with the same quant weights + runtime from canary. got truncated outputs, stop tokens missing. repro script: `python tools/repro.py --model ptq-20260312 --prompt tests/codegen/stopseq/long.py`

olga_qa: quick sample: input is a long function skeleton, expected completion ended with `"# END"` stopseq but model kept streaming extra unrelated text. logs show final token id sequence doesn't include EOS marker.

jun_engineer: running tokenization diff between ptq-20260312 tokenizer.json and baseline tokenizer.json now.

alex_infra: heads-up: we merged a tokenizer normalization change (lowercase-number-normalizer) in the model repo on 2026-03-11 to fix a separate eval flake. might be related.

jun_engineer: diff shows a new special mapping: token id 50256 used as "<num_norm>" in the new tokenizer. baseline had no mapping. PTQ packing pipeline assumes stable vocab indices; this adds a new ID and shifts subsequent ids by +1 in packed vocab table.

maria_research: aha — that shift would change stop-token IDs expected by decoding policy in the runtime. stop-seq defined by token ids, not strings, so mismatch causes missing stops.

sahil_eval: confirmed: mapping mismatch reproduces failure when runtime uses packed token ids from PTQ artifact but the decoding layer references stop ids from the canonical vocab.json. When we align them (use the packed vocab for decoding) stopseq works again.

alex_infra: root cause summary: tokenizer normalization change introduced a new special token id which shifted vocab indices in the PTQ-packed artifact. PTQ pipeline and runtime decoding were out-of-sync (packed-vocab vs canonical-vocab) causing stop-sequence/eos id misalignment. Not a quant kernel bug.

olga_qa: impact: codegen promptset stopseq failure spike (9.8%), some QA prompts also show early/late termination. Customer-facing generation APIs could return longer unexpected tails for a subset of models built with that tokenizer change. No data leak or hallucination increase measured.

maria_research: immediate mitigations?

alex_infra: 1) rollback PTQ build pipeline to use previous tokenizer mapping for serving (hotfix) — will cut ptq-rollback-20260312 within 30m. 2) Add strict check in PTQ pack step to verify vocab index stability vs canonical vocab (fail the build if shifts detected). 3) Add nightly token-diff test: compare token->id mapping for every new artifact.

jun_engineer: I'll owner 2 and 3. planning: add a unit test in packer that computes `sha256(vocab_table)` and asserts equality to baseline unless explicit vocab-change flag set. Also emit warning when special tokens are added.

olga_qa: 4) create a canary gating rule: any PTQ artifact with token-id diff > 0.1% fails canary automatically. 5) Roll out ptq-rollback to hosted and dedicated canaries before full production rollback.

sahil_eval: 6) update nightly eval to assert stop-seq coverage for codegen suite and fail the model-onboard job if regression > 2x baseline. I'll add a monitoring alert to paging for >5% regression.

maria_research: timeline + owners: alex infra -> roll forward rollback (30m), jun -> packer checks (EOD), sahil -> nightly guard (tomorrow AM), olga -> canary gating + QA verification (EOD).

alex_infra: deployed rollback to canary shard, running quick smoke. will promote after green. deploy-bot: `ptq-rollback-20260312` deployed to canary (shard-a).

deploy-bot: Deployment succeeded: ptq-rollback-20260312 -> canary-shard-a (2026-03-12T15:24:30Z).

jun_engineer: pushed packer test PR: CI will fail if vocab mismatch detected. link: https://git.internal/pr/4392

olga_qa: QA did a smoke run against canary — stop-seq samples look good. codegen failure rate on canary back down to 1.1%.

maria_research: follow-ups: document token-id stability requirement for model onboarding, add checklist item for tokenizer changes, and cross-team announcement when vocab maps change. Also schedule a postmortem writeup.

sahil_eval: adding a small test harness that converts stop-seq strings -> ids with both canonical and packed vocabs and asserts equality; will integrate into the onboard pipeline.

alex_infra: thanks everyone. closing loop: I'll coordinate prod rollback if canary remains green for 2 hours.

maria_research: great work. final note: this is a good example of a semantic change in tokenizer manifesting as a quality regression after quant/pack steps — we'll add it to onboarding risk matrix. :thumbsup:
